## Summary

I implemented the daily owner-registration limit in `OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner` (`src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/controller/v1/OwnerRestControllerV1.java`), the endpoint that handles `POST /api/owners`.

**Change:** After the registration date is resolved (defaulting to today when not supplied), the controller now checks how many existing owners already share that registration date. If 20 or more do, it returns `400 Bad Request` instead of creating the owner:

```java
if (hasReachedDailyRegistrationLimit(owner.getRegistrationDate())) {
    return new ResponseEntity<>(HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST);
}
```

The new `hasReachedDailyRegistrationLimit` helper counts owners whose `registrationDate` equals the target date and compares against the `MAX_OWNERS_PER_DAY = 20` constant, following the existing `findAllOwners()`-based idiom already used for the duplicate/customer-code logic in this controller.

**Test added:** `createOwnerRejectedWhenDailyLimitReached` seeds 20 owners registered today (each with a distinct telephone so they pass the uniqueness check), then POSTs a 21st unique owner and asserts `400`.

The check runs after the existing duplicate (`409 Conflict`) checks, so a duplicate still surfaces as a conflict and only genuinely-new owners are subject to the daily cap.

## Summary

I implemented the daily owner-registration limit in `OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner` (`src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/controller/v1/OwnerRestControllerV1.java`), the endpoint that handles `POST /api/owners`.

**Change:** After the registration date is resolved (defaulting to today when not supplied), the controller now checks how many existing owners already share that registration date. If 20 or more do, it returns `400 Bad Request` instead of creating the owner:

```java
if (hasReachedDailyRegistrationLimit(owner.getRegistrationDate())) {
    return new ResponseEntity<>(HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST);
}
```

The new `hasReachedDailyRegistrationLimit` helper counts owners whose `registrationDate` equals the target date and compares against the `MAX_OWNERS_PER_DAY = 20` constant, following the existing `findAllOwners()`-based idiom already used for the duplicate/customer-code logic in this controller.

**Test added:** `createOwnerRejectedWhenDailyLimitReached` seeds 20 owners registered today (each with a distinct telephone so they pass the uniqueness check), then POSTs a 21st unique owner and asserts `400`.

The check runs after the existing duplicate (`409 Conflict`) checks, so a duplicate still surfaces as a conflict and only genuinely-new owners are subject to the daily cap.
